reason: Both plans satisfy every hard requirement, but A sequences the verification-then-decision-then-rollback logic more cleanly (verify → go-live/rollback decision → reopen or roll back), whereas B places its rollback step after 'reopen traffic' even though rollback is triggered by earlier verification/smoke-test failures, making its numbered sequence read as internally inconsistent. A's rollback step is also more concretely actionable (repoint to intact on-prem DB, restore from pre-cutover backup if needed) versus B's vaguer 're-run the backup for audit purposes.'
